$comment: The parameters of every tool operation, and the sentence a model reads when it gets one wrong. Hand-written: this is the specification, and it covers the catalogue exhaustively — `every_catalog_operation_declares_its_parameters` fails if an operation is added without an entry here. `scripts/generate-command-surface.mjs` emits the Rust table that refuses a call, the signature the model is shown, and the addon-side guard for the operations the addon answers.
$commandComment: `command` is the addon command that answers the operation, and its absence — with `answeredBy: "rust"` in its place — means the operation never reaches the addon. Those are checked in Rust and deserialize into a typed request behind it; `every_rust_answered_operation_matches_its_request` holds this file to those structs.
$acceptsComment: `accepts` names a parameter the addon reads and the model is never told about. `scene` is the only one: every node command takes it and defaults it to the scene the editor already has open, so the desktop client passes it and the model has no reason to.
$gatedComment: `gated` is the sentence the user is shown before the agent may run this operation. Its absence means auto-allowed, so a new operation is allowed by default and has to be gated deliberately. It lives beside the parameters and the route because all three are facts about the same operation, and keeping the safety model in a table of its own meant a fifth place to look and a fifth thing to hold to the catalogue afterwards.
$aloneComment: `alone` narrows where an operation may sit in an `ops` list, and carries the sentence a caller reads when it gets that wrong. Every tool call is a list, so a model wanting three inspections writes one call rather than three. `scope: "repeat"` is the ordinary case: the operation may sit beside other operations, and may not appear twice, because it takes no parameters to vary or drives something the session owns exactly one of — the open scene, the running game, the undo stack, the dialog. The router runs a list in order, so a second one would only redo or undo the first. `scope: "exclusive"` is the debugger, where each answer decides what the next operation means, so the operation has to be the only entry of its call. Absence means the operation may appear as often as a list names it.
$vocabularyComment: `vocabularies` names a set of words a parameter accepts inside a structure, where `kind` cannot reach: `key` sits inside each entry of an `events` list. `accepted` is printed into the signature the model reads, because a generated signature is measurably more reliable than a sentence — see the note on `Kind` in tool_params.rs. `refused` is names the engine does not have, and it exists so `every_key_name_the_catalog_advertises_is_one_the_engine_knows` can prove the accepted list is meaningful rather than merely present. Both used to be written out twice, in English, inside two catalogue summaries, and read back out of the prose by a parser that split on the literal string “Accepted: ”.

entry.name: kind
entry.note: Which of the five an event is. Checked here rather than in the game: an event with no kind used to cross the socket and come back as `Input event kind '' is not supported`, which names nothing to send instead. One live turn wrote it 22 times.

entry.name: pressed
entry.note: Held down unless this says otherwise, so the release is a second event carrying false.

entry.name: button
entry.note: A mouse button by name - left, right, middle, wheel_up, wheel_down - or an index; a joypad button is an index.

params.name: frames
params.note: How many rendered frames to let pass. One when neither this nor `ms` is named.

params.name: ms
params.note: How long to let pass instead, in milliseconds. Held under ten seconds, which is what one request has.

params.name: maxPassages
params.note: How many passages come back is not a number the model can reason about, so it is settled here at four. gofer-rag takes it as a ceiling and applies it before pinning a chapter the question named, so the rescue survives it; replaying its 83 labelled questions through every ceiling, four keeps 79% of the bytes and loses no case, where three loses two. The desktop Docs panel sets its own bound, so the parameter stays accepted and unadvertised.
